name: Cool Grey
lede: Cool grey is a grey that leans toward blue, a distinction painters use constantly even though the swatch here is a pure neutral.

sections.title: How painters use it
sections.body: A painter's text on color and light treats cool and warm greys as working tools. For distant haze it suggests a light cool grey blended with a yellowish white at the same value [1]. In a large dark building the colors can move from a dark, cool grey at one end to a lighter, warmer grey at the other, and grey is called the "sauce" of a color scheme [2]. Transparent-media painters can also run a cool grey wash across a whole shadow area to key it down [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here is #A9A9A9, equal in red, green and blue, which has no hue and so is neither cool nor warm [4]. Coolness is relative: a grey looks cool next to a warmer one [4]. The same value is the web color `darkgrey`, and it also appears in the German RAL system from 1927 [4]. The ISCC-NBS system calls it "light gray", 5 units away [4]. Compare [[grey]] and [[white]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The ColorHub archive records chroma 0 and lightness near 69 out of 100 [4]. Contrast against white is 2.35 to 1 [4].
